turn.speech: Kleinkünstler, a deploy followed by 500s is a timeline, not a cause. A 500 means an unhandled error or a deliberate 500 from your code. Make one failing request and read the sb-error-code header plus the matching log line. Which value do you see?
turn.text:
Kleinkünstler, "500 after a deploy" is a symptom plus a timeline. It is not yet a cause. The deploy is the prime suspect, but secrets, config and upstream services can change at the same moment. I'll keep it a suspect until the evidence supports it.

## Incident model so far

| Field | Status |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Edge Function returns HTTP 500 |
| **Expected** | 2xx from the new version |
| **Scope** | Every request, per your report. Unverified: all callers, all routes, all methods? |
| **Timeline** | Started at a deploy. Unknown: what else changed (secrets, env, dependencies, upstream API)? |
| **Environment** | Unknown: hosted or local, CLI version, how it was deployed, runtime/imports |
| **Evidence** | None yet. You haven't shown me an error, a header or a log line. |

## What "500" can mean

Supabase's troubleshooting guide says a 500 from an Edge Function means one of two things. Either the function hit an unhandled JavaScript error, or your own code deliberately returned a 500. [1] Edge Function responses also carry an `sb-error-code` header that identifies the specific error. [3]

Two documented error codes fit "everything broke after deploy":
- **`BOOT_ERROR`**: the function failed to start. Common causes are syntax errors, import errors or missing dependencies, and invalid configuration. [2]
- **`EDGE_FUNCTION_ERROR`**: the function runs but throws an unhandled error or returns a 5XX. [3]

A resource-limit failure is less likely. The KB lists `WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT` as a 546, not a 500. [4] That is an inference from the page title. I haven't verified how every error code maps to a status.

## Hypotheses, ranked by current evidence

| # | Hypothesis | Why it fits | What would falsify it | Smallest test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Function fails to boot (bad import, syntax, config) | Breaks 100% of requests, and the timing matches a deploy | `sb-error-code` is something else, or the logs show handler code executing | Read `sb-error-code` and the boot logs |
| 2 | Handler throws on every request (missing secret, changed env var, new code path) | Also hits every request, and secrets are not deployed with the code | Logs show no exception, or the function returns 500 only for some inputs | Read the exception message and stack in the function logs |
| 3 | Code deliberately returns 500, e.g. a catch-all around a failing upstream call | Doc lists it as one of the two meanings. [1] | No `status: 500` in the code path, or the trace shows no upstream failure | Search the code for `status: 500` and read the `console.error` output |
| 4 | Resource limit | Possible after a bundle or dependency change | Status is 500, not 546 | Read the status and header |

The `sb-error-code` header and the function log line should rank these four in one step.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[500 on every request] --> B{sb-error-code header?}
  B -->|BOOT_ERROR| C[Startup problem: imports, syntax, config]
  B -->|EDGE_FUNCTION_ERROR| D{Exception in logs?}
  B -->|absent or other| E[Check status code and which layer answered]
  D -->|yes| F[Read message and stack: secret, env, code path]
  D -->|no explicit throw| G[Search code for deliberate status 500]
```

## Next evidence

Make one failing request and paste the response headers and body. Redact all keys and tokens first.

```bash
# Prerequisite: curl. Replace the placeholders; do not paste real keys back to me.
curl -i -X POST "https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/<function-name>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

Expected output is a status line, the headers, and a body. This request is read-only from your side, but it still executes the function. If your function has JWT verification on, add the same auth header your real callers send. A 401 would be a different finding, and a useful one.

Which `sb-error-code` header value (if any) does that response carry, and what is the first error line in the function logs for that same request?
